hero.caption: Spent on war since January 1, {year}
hero.methodology: Projected {year}, based on SIPRI {basedOnYear} actuals and a 5-year average growth rate. Actual figures are published annually in late April.

war.label: War
war.caption: Spent on war since January 1, {year}
war.methodology: Projected {year}, based on SIPRI {basedOnYear} actuals and a 5-year average growth rate. SIPRI's annual update was published 27 April 2026.

tobacco.label: Tobacco use
tobacco.caption: Lost to tobacco use since January 1, {year}
tobacco.methodology: USD 1.4 trillion per year — healthcare costs and lost productivity from tobacco use, ~1.8% of global GDP. Source: WHO / Goodchild et al. 2017.

fossil-fuels.label: Fossil fuels
fossil-fuels.caption: Subsidising fossil fuels since January 1, {year}
fossil-fuels.methodology: USD 7.4 trillion per year — explicit subsidies plus underpricing of climate and air-pollution costs. Source: IMF Working Paper 2025/270, 2024 data.

ai.label: AI
ai.caption: Poured into AI since January 1, {year}
ai.methodology: USD 770 billion projected for 2026 — Big-Five hyperscaler (Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle) AI/data-centre capex. Source: Epoch AI.

food-waste.label: Food wasted
food-waste.caption: Wasted on uneaten food since January 1, {year}
food-waste.methodology: USD 1 trillion per year — the direct economic value of food lost and wasted worldwide. Source: FAO Food Wastage Footprint, reaffirmed by UNEP Food Waste Index Report 2024.

advertising.label: Advertising
advertising.caption: Spent on advertising since January 1, {year}
advertising.methodology: USD 1.3 trillion projected for 2026 — total global advertising spend. Source: WARC Global Ad Trends, December 2025.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.counter: The counter projects this year's total global military spending based on the latest actual SIPRI figures multiplied by the 5-year average growth rate, then ticks in real time as a fraction of that yearly total based on seconds elapsed since January 1.
methodology.categories: Each humanitarian alternative is computed from authoritative sources (WHO, World Bank, UNICEF, Gavi, UN OCHA, UNESCO, IRENA, FAO). Cost units and citations are listed in each category’s “see sources” panel.
methodology.data: All data is open and lives in the public repository.
methodology.repoLabel: View data and source code on GitHub
